nodes.name: Whittaker character
nodes.statement: A Lie algebra homomorphism \(\psi:\ \mathfrak{n}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}\) is called a {\em Whittaker character}; the character \(\psi\) is {\em non-singular} if it is nonzero on the root spaces \(\mathfrak{g_\alpha}\) for all simple roots \(\alpha\in\Delta\).

nodes.name: Whittaker vector
nodes.statement: An element \(v\) of a \(\mathfrak{g\)-module \(V\) is said to be a {\em Whittaker vector of type} \(\psi\) if \(xv=\psi(x)v\) for all \(x\in\mathfrak{n}\).  The space of Whittaker vectors in \(V\) will be denoted by \(\hbox{Wh}\,V\).

nodes.name: Whittaker module
nodes.statement: Cyclic modules generated by Whittaker vectors of type \(\psi\) are called {\em Whittaker modules of type} \(\psi\) and are {\em singular} or {\em non-singular}, depending on whether \(\psi\) is singular or non-singular.  Each Whittaker module admits a unique Whittaker character, so the notions of singular and non-singular are well defined.

nodes.name: Set of simple roots \(\Delta_\psi\) for Whittaker character \(\psi\)
nodes.statement: Let \(\psi\) be a Whittaker character, and let \(\Delta_\psi\) be the set of simple roots \(\alpha\) for which \(\psi(\mathfrak{g_\alpha)\neq 0\).

nodes.name: Reductive subalgebra \(\mathfrak{l}_\psi\)
nodes.statement: We write \(\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_\psi\) for the reductive subalgebra generated by the sum of \({\mathfrak h\) and the root spaces \(\mathfrak{g_\alpha\) with \(\pm\alpha\in \Delta_\psi\).

nodes.name: Triangular decomposition of \(\mathfrak{l}\)
nodes.statement: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak{l}\) has a triangular decomposition \(\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_-\oplus{\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak{l}_+\), where \(\mathfrak{l}_+\) and \(\mathfrak{l}_-\) are the intersections of \(\mathfrak{l}\) with the positive and negative root spaces of \(\mathfrak{g\), respectively.

nodes.name: Parabolic subalgebra \(\mathfrak{p}\)
nodes.statement: The centre \(\mathfrak{z}\) of \(\mathfrak{l}\) lies in {\mathfrak h\), and the corresponding parabolic subalgebra \(\mathfrak{l}+\mathfrak{n}\) will be denoted by \(\mathfrak{p}\).

nodes.name: Decomposition of \(\mathfrak{p}\)
nodes.statement: The subalgebra \(\mathfrak{p}\) has a unique \(\operatorname{ad}{\mathfrak h\)-stable decomposition \(\mathfrak{p}=\mathfrak{l}\oplus\mathfrak{m}\), and \(\mathfrak{g=\overline{\mathfrak{m}}\oplus\mathfrak{l}\oplus\mathfrak{m}\), where \(\overline{\mathfrak{m}}\) is the Lie subalgebra spanned by the root spaces \(\mathfrak{g_{-\alpha}\) for which \(\mathfrak{g_\alpha\) is contained in \(\mathfrak{m}\).

nodes.name: Definition of \(Y_{\Omega,\psi}\)
nodes.statement:
For an arbitrary central character \(\Omega:\,Z(\mathfrak{l})\rightarrow\mathbb{C}\), consider the induced \(\mathfrak{l}\)-module
$$Y_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{l})\otimes_{Z(\mathfrak{l})U(\mathfrak{l}_+)}\mathbb{C}v_{\Omega,\psi},$$
where \(Z(\mathfrak{l})U(\mathfrak{l}_+)=Z(\mathfrak{l})\otimes U(\mathfrak{l}_+)\) acts by the characters \(\Omega\) and \(\psi\) on the \(1\)-dimensional space spanned by the vector \(v_{\Omega,\psi}\).

$$M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}.$$
